output.summary: A small to medium-sized tree native to New Caledonia, Papua New Guinea and coastal eastern Australia, it often grows in swamps, floodplains and beside waterways. Its trunk has thick, peeling papery bark, while cream or white bottlebrush-like flowers appear from late spring to autumn.
output.edibilityNote: Traditionally, nectar was washed into water and consumed as a beverage; its flowers also yield a strongly flavoured honey.
